text:
alex: Quick heads-up — ran an nsys timeline on the TRT-vLLM wrapper for the 13B endpoint, and the profile looks... weird. large tail in wrapper_invoke and repeated small trtEngineCreate calls.
priya: ugh. is this the hotfix commit from yesterday? which hash? :eyes:
alex: yeah that one — commit 7f3a12d changed the kernel selection threshold in engine selector. repro cmd I used: 
```
nsys profile --sample=none --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --output=trace_trt_vllm ./run_invoke.sh --model redwood/13b --batch 8 --seq 1024 --requests 120
```
brandon: can you paste the top timeline summary? rough % breakdown is fine.
alex: roughly: wrapper_total ~48%, scheduler_lock ~18%, trtExecute kernels ~22%, memcpy HtoD/DtoH ~7%, small kernels (layout/transpose) ~5%. But also ~12x tiny trtEngineCreate spikes, each ~6-8ms — these look like engine fallback builds when batch shape changes.
maria: engine create during serving?? That will blow latency. are we seeing different shape signatures due to KV cache lengths?
alex: yup — when requests have variable prefix lengths, the scheduler is changing sequence_length and we end up trying to select an engine variant. selector logic currently does an on-the-fly fallback to build another engine if no exact kernel match.
sean: does TRT cache engines on device or in host memory? could be thrashing if cleanup runs.
priya: TRT caches per-process but our wrapper sometimes calls destroy on mismatch to avoid OOM. after the selector change it seems we destroy+recreate more aggressively.
brandon: can we confirm which kernels are taking most time in the created engines? nvprof/nvtx markers?
alex: added NVTX markers around selector and engine build. snippet: 
```
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH("selector:choose_kernel");
// choose kernel
NVTX_RANGE_POP();
NVTX_RANGE_PUSH("engine:create");
// trt engine build
NVTX_RANGE_POP();
```
alex: nsys shows engine:create spans correlate with heavy cudaMalloc/cudaFree and cuBLAS/cuDNN workspace setups. not pure kernel time but memory setup + JIT-like operations.
maria: that explains wrapper_total ballooning. scheduler_lock being high suggests serializing while engine created. we should never block global scheduler on engine builds.
sean: agree. two quick mitigation ideas: 1) pre-warm engine variants for common sequence lengths at startup (background builds), 2) make build async so scheduler can route to fallback model variant temporarily.
priya: both good. also batcher heuristics: batcher currently sends batches grouped by arrival time, but not by sequence_length. we could change grouping key to (batch_size, seq_len_bucket) to reduce shape variability.
brandon: how many distinct seq_lengths are we seeing? alex?
alex: histogram in trace: seq_len buckets: 64: 18%, 128: 23%, 256: 20%, 512: 14%, 1024: 12%, >1024: 13%. So lots of variety.
maria: that many buckets explains why engine cache miss rate is high. maybe quantize seq_len into fewer buckets (round to next power-of-two or fixed cutpoints).
priya: will also reduce memcpy churn: when seq_len smaller than engine max, we do padding + memcpy per request. fewer engine variants reduces memcpy patterns.
sean: can you also check KV cache behavior? maybe we copy KV to host for some path then back to device repeatedly.
alex: good call — nsys shows periodic memcpy DtoH around same times as engine create, but also smaller DtoH during regular invokes. I sampled a request timeline: 
```
[request start]
wrapper_invoke enter
check engine -> miss -> trigger async build
serialize request -> place into fallback queue (FP16 variant)
scheduler_lock wait 12ms
fallback engine run (trtExecute) ~18ms
on build complete: swap engine pointer
[request end]
```
maria: fallback queue + lock wait indicates build path still blocks scheduling decision. we need a non-blocking path.
brandon: for immediate next steps: can we (A) add async engine build + builder threadpool, (B) change selector to prefer existing compatible engine variants (even if suboptimal perf) as fallback, and (C) update batcher to cluster by seq_len_bucket?
priya: + run another nsys with --capture-range=process to avoid capture noise and get per-request NVTX timeline. also capture `nvprof --profile-child-processes` for kernels that are spawned separately.
sean: I can prototype async builder threadpool. will need a thread-safe engine registry. alex can add NVTX markers for queue enqueue/dequeue and builder events.
alex: will do. i'll also create a small perf test that simulates arrival distribution from prod logs (mix of seq lengths) and run it in staging to validate cache hit rate. repro script in tools/perf/sim_batcher.sh (will post).
maria: let's also add a regression test that fails if engine create count per 10k reqs > threshold (e.g., 50). Catch this in CI for runtime selector changes.
priya: logging: add a metric trt_engine_build_count with tags model, seq_len_bucket, node. Push to metrics pipeline so we can alert on increases.
brandon: owner list: async build PR -> sean. selector rollback/heuristic -> priya + alex. metrics/regression -> maria. perf sim -> alex. timeline re-run -> alex.
sean: I'll start on threadpool today. expect a draft PR by EOD.
alex: re-running nsys with nvtx markers after smaller run — will paste updated flame in this thread. thanks all. :thumbsup:
runtime-bot: deploy hook: perf-test cluster scaled to 6 nodes for profiling run
priya: noted, thanks runtime-bot. :rocket:
